statement: Content is one ContentScope aggregate per workspace (plus one public scope for hub modules). It serializes explicit pins against garbage collection sweeps, and the blocks themselves are not event sourced. Files and databases are single-writer streams whose changes commit atomically with the run step that caused them. The file system is a chain of root CIDs. A database is a SQLite working copy that can always be rebuilt from its snapshot plus the ordered statements after it, with Rui's (run, step) table acting as the outbox that keeps the two in step.

event_changes.why: RestoreDatabase is needed to recover a corrupt working copy, to roll back a bad migration, and to rebuild after erasure. It moves the database to a snapshot plus sequence and must be a fact in the stream, otherwise later statements replay against the wrong base.
BlockIntegrityFailed has no closing event. Auditors need to see that a missing or corrupt block was restored from a verified source (replica or hub), and when.

hotspot_resolutions.resolution: Both, with clear roles. The event stream databases/<ws>/<name> is the record, and the SQLite file is a working copy that is never rebuilt routinely, only on restore, corruption or point-in-time queries. Write path, single writer per database: (1) begin a SQLite transaction, (2) apply the statement, (3) insert (run, step, seq, statement text, parameters CID) into a cloud-owned _cloud_outbox table (Rui's idempotency table, now also an outbox), (4) commit, (5) append DatabaseStatementExecuted at expected version seq-1 in the same ledger append as the run's EffectResultRecorded. On recovery, any outbox rows above the stream version are appended, which makes the effect exactly-once without rebuilds. A unique (run, step) pair makes retries no-ops. Statements must be deterministic: random(), datetime('now'), last_insert_rowid-dependent writes and similar are rejected or bound from journaled Now/Random. Schema DDL is just a statement. DatabaseSnapshotTaken stores a VACUUM INTO copy as chunked blocks plus a logical digest (hash of rows ordered by primary key per table), because SQLite file bytes are not deterministic. A weekly verification rebuilds the previous snapshot plus statements and compares digests. Reads (SQLiteQuery) are not database events; their results are journaled in the run as result CIDs.

Dedup is per workspace scope only. Each workspace has its own ContentScope, and blocks are encrypted at rest with the scope's key (and with subject keys for identified personal data), so identical bytes in two workspaces are two blocks and cross-tenant confirmation-of-file is impossible. The only shared scope is `public`: hub modules and signed releases, which are already public and are stored unencrypted with global dedup. Legal holds and erasure act on roots and keys, never on individual blocks. A hold pins roots inside one scope. A block encrypted under a subject key is shared only by data of that same subject, so shredding cannot destroy another scope's data. records refuses SubjectKeyShredded (ErasureRefusedUnderLegalHold) while any held root references a block under that key. Remaining risk, accepted and documented: events keep plaintext UnixFS CIDs so file semantics hold. A small personal payload could be confirmed by guessing after shredding, so personal payloads under 4 KiB are stored inline encrypted rather than as plaintext-addressed blocks.

invariants: a root is pinned only once every block under it is present and verifies against its CID
only the holder that pinned a root (hold id, tag, operator) can release it
pins and sweeps are serialized in this stream: a sweep records its mark epoch, and any root pinned or referenced after the epoch is excluded from that sweep
a block younger than the grace period (24h) is never swept, which protects blocks written before their event is appended
at most one sweep in progress per scope
blocks of the public scope are never swept while any release references them
one rebuild at a time per read model
a rebuild records the projector CID and the global position or snapshot it started from
the read model only serves queries once caught up to the position recorded at rebuild start
every change names expected previous_root, which must equal the head, otherwise the command is retried against the new head (the paths do not conflict) or rejected
paths are normalized and absolute, and the root cannot be deleted
file bytes are put as chunked blocks (256 KiB) before the event is appended; the event holds only CIDs
a change made by a run commits in the same ledger append as that run's EffectResultRecorded (internal effect, exactly-once)
restore targets must be roots that are still live (in LiveRoots)
single writer; statements apply in stream order, and the stream version equals the outbox sequence
(run, step) is unique, so a retried write is a no-op
only deterministic statements are accepted
raw statements require a shell with with_databases; dataclip statements carry the dataclip CID
a snapshot names the sequence it covers and its logical digest
a restore names its snapshot and sequence, and every statement after it applies to that base
the invoked version is the dataclip CID in the configuration applied at invocation
a dataclip runs with its own shell, recorded on the event, not the caller's
a read-only dataclip emits no DatabaseStatementExecuted
